title: Body Composition Data in Obesity Drug Development: FDA and EMA Review of DXA and MRI Endpoints and Weight-Loss Efficacy Benchmarks
summary: How FDA and EMA review DXA and MRI body-composition data in obesity drug programs, and the weight-loss efficacy benchmarks that still decide approval.
body_markdown:
## Body composition in obesity drug development: how FDA and EMA review DXA and MRI data, and the weight-loss benchmarks that still govern approval


Body-composition data (fat mass, lean mass and visceral adiposity, measured by DXA, CT or MRI) are now standard in obesity programs. Neither FDA nor EMA treats them as an approval endpoint. Both agencies still decide approvability on total body weight. They read body composition mainly as confirmation that the weight lost is fat rather than muscle or body water. This article summarizes the current guidance positions, the efficacy benchmarks, and how reviewers handled DXA and imaging data for semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide, phentermine/topiramate, naltrexone/bupropion and others.


### Key takeaways


- **FDA benchmark.** FDA's January 2025 draft guidance considers a weight-reduction drug effective if, after 1 year at the maintenance dosage, the difference in mean percentage weight reduction versus control is at least 5% and statistically significant[94](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=94) . The draft says responder analyses are "generally not recommended"[396](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=396) . This drops the categorical (≥5% responder) alternative that the 2007 draft offered[465](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=465) .
- **EMA benchmark.** The current EMA weight-management guideline treats statistically significant, placebo-corrected weight loss of at least 5% of baseline weight after 12 months as a valid primary efficacy criterion. Responder analyses at ≥5% and ≥10% are still expected[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=63) .
- **FDA on body composition.** FDA asks for DXA (or a suitable alternative) in a representative sample, "to ensure that drug-induced or biologic-induced weight reduction is caused primarily by a reduction in fat content, not lean-body mass"[256](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=256) . FDA notes that fat has typically made up 60% to 90% of weight lost in drug trials, and that the accompanying lean-mass loss "has not been considered adverse"[280](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=280) .
- **EMA on body composition.** EMA asks for central adiposity (waist circumference or waist-to-hip ratio) as a secondary endpoint. It says DEXA, MRI or CT "should preferably be included" to show appropriate loss of body fat as distinct from muscle or body water[411](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=411)[412](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=412) .
- **Body-composition claims.** Under FDA's draft, a sponsor wanting an efficacy claim based on body-composition change must consult FDA early to agree on the clinical condition being treated[282](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=282) .


### Efficacy benchmarks that still govern approval


#### FDA: from two benchmarks to one


FDA's 2007 draft guidance, *Developing Products for Weight Management* , is quoted in the liraglutide (Saxenda) statistical review. It offered two alternative benchmarks after 1 year of treatment[464](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=464)[465](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=465) :


- **Mean-based:** a placebo-subtracted difference in mean weight loss of at least 5%, statistically significant[465](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=465) .
- **Categorical:** at least 35% of subjects on drug losing ≥5% of baseline weight, about double the placebo proportion, with a statistically significant difference[465](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=465) .


The January 7, 2025 draft guidance, *Obesity and Overweight: Developing Drugs and Biological Products for Weight Reduction* , keeps the mean-based test and drops the categorical one:


- **Primary endpoint:** efficacy in adults "should be assessed by analyses of mean percentage change from baseline body weight in the investigational drug group versus the control group"[484](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=484) .
- **Benchmark:** at least a 5% difference in mean percentage weight reduction versus control, statistically significant, after 1 year at the maintenance dosage[94](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=94) .
- **Responder analyses:** "generally not recommended". Sponsors who want a responder endpoint should consult the Agency[396](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=396) .
- **Trial design:** randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials, with the drug added to diet and physical-activity advice[95](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=95) .
- **Safety database:** 3,000 participants on drug and at least 1,500 on placebo, treated for at least 1 year at the maintenance dosage, generally across two adequate and well-controlled trials[77](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=77)[96](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=96) .
- **Secondary endpoints:** should include blood pressure, lipoprotein lipids, fasting glucose, and A1C in subjects with type 2 diabetes[485](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=485) . Waist circumference "may be evaluated as a secondary endpoint", and whether it can go in labeling depends on data quality[486](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=486) .
- **Estimands:** FDA generally recommends including treatment-policy estimand analyses, measuring all subjects regardless of intercurrent events[488](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=488) . Examples of intercurrent events are treatment discontinuation, prohibited or additional medications, and corrective surgery[489](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=489) .


The 2025 document is a draft labeled "Not for Implementation", and guidance recommendations are generally not legally binding[92](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=92)[93](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=93) . Until it is finalized, sponsors should expect FDA to apply the mean-based standard. They should not assume the 2007 categorical alternative is still accepted.


For comparison, CDRH's final March 2026 device guidance on weight-loss indications uses different benchmarks. For a "weight loss" indication, it recommends mean % total body-weight loss superiority of at least 5% over control. For any weight-loss indication, at least 50% of treated participants should achieve ≥5% total body-weight loss[101](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=101) . Device and drug programs should not borrow each other's thresholds.


#### EMA: 5% placebo-corrected at 12 months, with ≥10% responders still scrutinized


The EMA *Guideline on clinical evaluation of medicinal products used in weight management* (catalogued as 2017) sets these expectations:


- **Primary endpoint:** body weight reduction. A valid primary criterion is statistically significant placebo-corrected weight loss of at least 5% of baseline after 12 months[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=63) .
- **Reporting:** weight loss in kg and in percent, plus responder analyses at ≥5% and ≥10%. Patients who leave before 12 months count as non-responders[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=63) .
- **Confirmatory trials:** randomized, placebo-controlled and double-blind[300](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=300) . Most confirmatory trials should last at least 12 months. A randomized withdrawal design may help show how long the effect lasts[301](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=301) .
- **Population:** BMI ≥30 kg/m², or a lower BMI (e.g., ≥27 kg/m²) with weight-related risk factors. Programs should include relevant samples with class II and class III obesity[299](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=299) .


The earlier 2008 EMA guideline was stricter. It required at least 10% weight loss from baseline *and* at least 5% more loss than placebo, or >10% loss at 12 months as a responder-based alternative[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=66) .


Parameter FDA (2025 draft) EMA (current guideline)


Primary endpoint Mean % change from baseline body weight vs control[484](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=484) Body weight reduction; placebo-corrected ≥5% at 12 months is a valid criterion[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=63)


Benchmark ≥5% mean difference, statistically significant, after 1 year at maintenance dose[94](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=94) ≥5% placebo-corrected loss, statistically significant, at 12 months[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=63)


Responder analyses Generally not recommended; consult FDA[396](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=396) Expected at ≥5% and ≥10%; early dropouts are non-responders[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=63)


Body composition DXA or suitable alternative in a representative sample[256](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=256) DEXA, MRI or CT preferably included as secondary endpoints[411](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=411)[412](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=412)


Central adiposity Waist circumference may be a secondary endpoint[486](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=486) Waist circumference or waist-to-hip ratio should be documented as secondary endpoints[411](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=411)


#### How the benchmarks have been applied


**FDA reviews**


- **Contrave (naltrexone/bupropion).** Under "Benchmarks for clinical significance", the reviewer found the placebo-adjusted mean effect somewhat below 5% in all four phase 3 studies. The 95% CIs included 5%, so the reviewer cautioned against concluding that the true effect was below 5%[233](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=233) . The same reviewer called the 35%/double-placebo categorical benchmark unnecessarily complicated and suggested an odds-ratio approach[233](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=233) .
- **Meridia (sibutramine).** The reviewer concluded that 15 to 30 mg doses gave mean weight loss at least 5 percentage points greater than placebo[232](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=232) .
- **Wegovy (semaglutide 2.4 mg).** Trial 4373 (STEP 1) showed −14.85% vs −2.41% at week 68, an estimated treatment difference of −12.44 percentage points[434](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=434)[435](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=435) . In the Clinical Review, 86.4% vs 31.5% achieved ≥5% loss[436](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=436)[437](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=437) . The Deputy Division Director called the results "clinically meaningful and statistically robust"[441](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=441) .
- **Zepbound (tirzepatide).** At 15 mg, the placebo-adjusted differences were −17.8 points in SURMOUNT-1 and −11.6 points in SURMOUNT-2. Responder rates at ≥5% loss were 90.9% and 82.8%, versus 34.5% and 32.5% on placebo[343](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=343)[344](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=344)[345](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=345) . The reviewer called the primary endpoint consistent with Division expectations[346](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=346) .


Incretin-era effects now exceed the 5% threshold by a wide margin. The benchmark remains the regulatory floor, not the competitive bar.


**CHMP assessments**


- **Saxenda (liraglutide).** CHMP called a 5.2% placebo-subtracted loss, with 30.5% vs 8.4% achieving ≥10% loss, clinically relevant and in line with the guideline[153](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=153) . It separately accepted a 5% loss after 12 weeks on 3.0 mg/day as an individual-patient stopping rule[154](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=154) .
- **Mysimba (naltrexone/bupropion).** The trials used ≥5% responders as co-primary, while CHMP's guideline defined ≥10% as the responder variable[274](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=274) . CHMP accepted the mismatch because ≥10% was a prespecified secondary endpoint[275](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=275) . The ≥10% responder rates were 18.5% to 41.5% vs 5.7% to 20.2% on placebo (FAS/LOCF), and 13.4% to 30.3% vs 4.2% to 17.3% under the more conservative all-randomized/BOCF approach[157](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=157) . CHMP noted that in the BOCF analyses the placebo difference did not exceed 5%, yet judged efficacy modest but clinically relevant[155](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=155)[156](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=156)[157](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=157)[158](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=158)[159](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=159) .
- **Imcivree (setmelanotide).** CHMP accepted a ≥10% responder primary endpoint tested against a 5% historical responder rate, an approach that fits rare monogenic obesity[160](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=160)[161](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=161) .
- **Wegovy and Mounjaro.** CHMP reported a 12.4% placebo-adjusted loss in STEP 1[163](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=163) . It found tirzepatide's weight-management endpoints in accordance with the 2016 guideline[164](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=164) .


### What the agencies expect on body composition


#### FDA


The 2025 draft sets out FDA's reasoning:


- **Lean-mass loss is expected.** Lean-mass loss "is observed after weight reduction in patients with obesity or overweight regardless of intervention type (lifestyle, bariatric surgery, or pharmacotherapy)". People with obesity also have more lean mass than lean people, including more muscle, organ mass and total body water[279](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=279) .
- **It has not been considered adverse.** In pharmacological trials, fat has typically made up 60% to 90% of weight lost, and the accompanying lean-mass reduction "has not been considered adverse"[280](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=280) .
- **Adults.** A representative sample needs baseline and follow-up DXA or a suitable alternative[256](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=256) .
- **Pediatrics.** Baseline and follow-up DXA or a suitable alternative "should be obtained in pediatric subjects"[281](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=281) .
- **Body-composition claims.** These need early FDA consultation. Designing trials with endpoints that measure how a patient feels, functions or survives to support such a claim is outside the guidance's scope[282](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=282) .


The draft does not specifically recommend MRI or CT. It does not ask for visceral fat or bone mineral density as named measurements[258](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=258) . It also sets no separate physical-function assessment requirement[254](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=254) .


#### EMA


Under "4.2.1 Body weight related secondary endpoints", the EMA guideline says central adiposity (waist circumference or waist-to-hip ratio) "should be documented as secondary endpoints". It adds that DEXA, MRI or CT "should preferably be included as secondary endpoints to demonstrate that weight loss is associated with appropriate loss of body fat (as distinct from muscle or body water)"[411](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=411)[412](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=412) . EMA's rationale is that central adiposity predicts comorbidity risk and that waist circumference independently predicts risk[410](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=410) .


The 2008 guideline described DXA as "a direct, accurate, and precise measure of lean body mass and total fat mass" and listed CT and MRI as alternatives[36](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=36)[37](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=37)[387](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=387) . The 2009 paediatric addendum makes body composition analysis, by a validated method in a representative sample, "necessary" to confirm that weight reduction comes mainly from fat and not lean body mass[39](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=39) .


Compared with FDA's draft, EMA explicitly names visceral and central adiposity measures and MRI/CT as acceptable methods. FDA's draft is limited to DXA "or a suitable alternative".


### How reviewers interpreted DXA and imaging data, product by product


#### Semaglutide 2.4 mg (Wegovy)


FDA's clinical review described a DXA substudy in 140 U.S. participants in Trial 4373 (95 on semaglutide, 45 on placebo)[169](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=169)[170](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=170) . The EPAR reports the same substudy as supportive, through week 68[205](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=205) . Changes were as follows (FDA figures; EPAR figures agree after rounding)[207](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=207)[208](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=208) :


Measure Semaglutide Placebo Difference


Total fat mass −8.36 kg −1.37 kg −6.99 kg[171](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=171)


Lean body mass −5.26 kg −1.83 kg −3.43 kg[174](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=174)


Lean mass, % of total body mass +3.04 points +0.09 points +2.94 points[175](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=175)[173](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=173)


Visceral fat mass −0.36 kg −0.10 kg −0.27 kg[176](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=176)


Visceral fat, % of total fat −1.99 points −0.01 points −1.98 points[177](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=177)


- **FDA.** The reviewer concluded that the weight lost was mainly fat, not lean mass. The reviewer also said the substudy added no benefit beyond the primary and key secondary endpoints. Its CIs were descriptive, outside Type I error control[178](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=178)[173](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=173) .
- **CHMP.** CHMP called the fat and visceral-fat reductions statistically significant. It noted that lean mass fell in kilograms but rose as a share of body weight[209](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=209) . CHMP read this as better body composition, with most weight lost as fat, including visceral fat[210](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=210) .


#### Tirzepatide (Zepbound / Mounjaro)


- **Substudy.** FDA's SURMOUNT-1 DXA addendum enrolled 255 participants, with scans at baseline and week 72[45](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=45)[46](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=46) .
- **Fat mass.** −33.9% on pooled tirzepatide vs −8.2% on placebo, a difference of −25.7 points[50](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=50) .
- **Lean mass.** −10.9% vs −2.6%, a difference of −8.3 points[51](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=51) .
- **FDA's view.** The reviewer said FDA's main reason for assessing body composition is *safety* : to confirm that weight loss is mostly fat. Fat-mass loss about threefold greater than lean-mass loss was "consistent with other approved weight-management medications" and "not a safety concern"[52](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=52) .
- **CHMP's view.** CHMP considered loss of fat mass, rather than body water or muscle, desirable. It also valued the waist-circumference reduction because of the cardiovascular risk linked to central adiposity[25](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=25) . The EU product information reports an accompanying reduction in visceral fat without a separate number[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=22) . A PK/PD body-weight model separately attributed about three times as much weight loss to fat as to fat-free mass[23](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=23)[24](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=24) .


The cardiac MRI addendum in the tirzepatide dossier measured pericardial fat in HFpEF. It is not a weight-management visceral-fat MRI result[26](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=26) .


#### Liraglutide 3.0 mg (Saxenda)


FDA's review of the 20-week DEXA substudy in trial 1807 reported ranges across doses, not 3.0 mg alone[212](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=212)[213](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=213) :


- **Fat mass:** reductions of 5.0 to 6.9 kg on liraglutide vs 4.4 kg on placebo[214](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=214) .
- **Lean mass:** reductions of 0.5 to 1.5 kg vs 0.6 kg[215](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=215) .
- **Share of weight lost as fat:** 75% to 92% on liraglutide vs about 88% on placebo. Most differences were not nominally significant[216](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=216)[217](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=217) .


The EPAR summary says weight loss was primarily from fat rather than lean body mass[308](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=308) .


#### Phentermine/topiramate ER (Qsymia)


DEXA was an "other efficacy endpoint" in small subsets of OB-302 and OB-303[377](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=377) . Percent fat fell and percent lean rose in every arm, including placebo. Only the OB-303 active arms reached nominal significance; at 15/92 mg, fat changed by −4.2 points and lean by +3.8 points (both p<0.0001)[378](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=378)[385](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=385) . When FDA asked for bone mineral density, the sponsor explained that the scans had not imaged the anatomic sites needed for reliable BMD measurement[386](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=386) . Programs that want both body-composition and BMD data should design DXA acquisition for both from the start.


#### Naltrexone/bupropion (Contrave / Mysimba)


- **U.S. label.** DEXA in 124 patients showed fat mass falling 4.7 kg on Contrave vs 1.4 kg on placebo at week 52[125](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=125) .
- **EU product information.** It adds multislice CT (34 vs 24 subjects). DEXA showed greater reductions in total body fat and visceral adipose tissue, with a rise in percentage lean mass[272](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=272) . This is one of the clearer label statements of a visceral-fat finding from cross-sectional imaging.


#### Other precedents


- **Sibutramine (Meridia).** DEXA showed −1.8 vs −0.2 kg fat and −0.8 vs −0.3 kg lean mass[126](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=126)[127](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=127) . The label reported greater total and truncal fat loss, with no statistically significant difference in lean mass between groups[128](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=128)[129](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=129) .
- **Diazoxide choline (Vykat XR).** DEXA showed a trend toward *increased* lean mass[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=133) . The reviewer cautioned that DXA lean mass includes body water, and checked whether drug-related fluid retention affected the result. Excluding eight subjects did not materially change it[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=133)[134](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=134) . Any drug with fluid effects needs the same check.


#### Lean mass in older or sarcopenic patients


The Wegovy, Mounjaro and Saxenda EPAR passages reviewed treat lean-mass loss as part of a favorable body-composition shift. None of them flags elderly or sarcopenic patients as a specific CHMP concern[209](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=209)[306](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=306)[307](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=307)[308](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=308) . FDA's draft guidance likewise does not set a separate physical-function requirement[254](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=254) .


### Visceral adiposity as a primary endpoint: the tesamorelin precedent


The clearest FDA precedent for visceral fat as a *primary* endpoint is outside general obesity: tesamorelin (Egrifta) for HIV lipodystrophy.


- **Endpoint.** The primary endpoint was percent change in visceral adipose tissue (VAT) at week 26 by CT at L4 to L5[365](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=365) . VAT was measured as cross-sectional area from a single 5-mm CT slice[366](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=366) .
- **Results.** Mean treatment differences were −31 cm² and −21 cm² across the two studies[368](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=368) .
- **FDA's view.** The Division accepted VAT as a primary endpoint because of evidence linking visceral adiposity to cardiometabolic risk factors. It accepted an 8% VAT reduction as clinically meaningful for powering[371](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=371) . The Cross Discipline Team Leader also wrote that VAT is not fully validated as a surrogate for cardiovascular risk reduction, with no direct link yet shown between lowering VAT and cardiovascular morbidity or mortality[369](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=369)[370](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=370) .


That reasoning carries over to any obesity sponsor considering an MRI-based visceral or ectopic fat claim. Under FDA's 2025 draft, such a claim needs early agreement on the clinical condition and on endpoints that reflect how patients feel, function or survive[282](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=282) . No CHMP assessment of tesamorelin was found in the EPAR collection.


### Implications for development programs


- **Treat total body weight as the approval endpoint in both regions.** For FDA, power on mean percentage change and the ≥5% placebo-adjusted difference at 1 year[94](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=94)[484](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=484) . For EMA, also prespecify ≥5% and ≥10% responder analyses, counting early dropouts as non-responders[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=63) . The Mysimba assessment shows CHMP will examine the ≥10% responder result closely even when it is secondary[274](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=274)[275](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=275) .
- **Build DXA into a representative subset.** Both agencies use it mainly to confirm that weight lost is mostly fat[256](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=256)[411](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=411) . Reviewers have compared fat-to-lean loss ratios across the class. The tirzepatide review calls a roughly threefold ratio consistent with approved products[52](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=52) , and FDA's draft cites fat making up 60% to 90% of weight lost[280](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=280) .
- **Add CT or MRI for visceral or central adiposity if EU labeling of visceral-fat effects matters.** EMA names these methods explicitly[411](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=411)[412](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=412) , and the Mysimba EU product information shows such data can reach the SmPC[272](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=272) .
- **Plan body-composition claims as separate programs.** FDA's draft treats them as needing their own clinical condition and patient-relevant endpoints[282](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=282) . The Egrifta review shows FDA will question whether a visceral-fat reduction translates into clinical benefit[370](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=370) .
- **Control DXA confounders.** Body water and fluid retention affect lean-mass readings[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=133) . Scans designed for body composition may not give usable BMD data[386](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/body-composition-in-obesity-drug-development?showSourceNumber=386) .


Open questions worth exploring further include: how FDA's final weight-reduction guidance will handle body-composition claims; whether muscle-preserving agents will be held to functional endpoints; and how CHMP will assess lean-mass loss in older adults as incretin and amylin combinations come forward.
